word_bank.example: The French Revolution changed the political order of Europe forever.
The Declaration of Independence was signed in 1776.
Many countries celebrate their independence with parades and fireworks.
The Constitution is the highest law of the United States.
Martin Luther King Jr. fought for civil rights for all Americans.
The Lincoln Memorial is one of the most famous landmarks in Washington D.C.
The Industrial Era transformed how people lived and worked.
They built a monument to honour the soldiers who died in the war.
Our cultural heritage connects us to the generations who came before us.
Abraham Lincoln's legacy continues to inspire people around the world.

stage_2_story.text_en: Last summer, David took his son to the national history museum. It was a special trip — a chance to explore the heritage of their country together. In the first hall, they stood before a large monument honouring soldiers who had fought for civil rights and equality. A guide explained that the struggle had been a turning point, a true revolution in the way society treated its citizens. They moved on to a room dedicated to the era of independence, where an old copy of the original Declaration was displayed behind glass. David read it slowly, explaining each line to his son. Further inside, they found the original Constitution, framed and lit by soft museum lights. Outside the building stood a landmark bronze statue of a founding leader. As they walked home, David told his son about the legacy these people had left behind — courage, justice, and the belief that every person deserves dignity. His son listened carefully, already planning to write about it at school.

questions.question: Where did David take his son?
What was in the first hall of the museum?
What did the guide describe as a turning point?
What did David read slowly to his son?
How was the Constitution displayed?
options: (b) Framed and lit by soft museum lights

questions.question: What stood outside the museum building?
What era was one room in the museum dedicated to?
What did David tell his son about on the way home?
options: (c) The legacy left by the founding leaders

questions.question: What three values did David say the leaders left behind?
What was the son planning to do after the visit?
options: (d) Draw a picture of the monument
